scope: Isolated training comparator prototype only. Cortex suspended; no shared source, Git, service, UI, persistence or official exam implementation.

findings.title: Invalid runtime keys can become blank or correct instead of throwing
additionalCases: Sparse five-element option array with a hole
findings.expected: Reject invalid key before interpreting even a blank answer. Runtime discriminant must be choice or number; five option IDs must actually be strings and valid A-E identifiers for this proposal.
findings.fix: Validate runtime shape before blank handling; inspect sparse arrays via spread/Array.from, not Array.some directly, which skips holes.

findings.title: Implicit leading zero consumes a written-digit slot
findings.fix: Change digits=(match[2]??'0')+fraction to digits=(match[2]??'')+fraction; the grammar guarantees a non-empty fractional sequence in this branch.

confirmedBehavior: Exact BigInt cross-products, no parseFloat/eval or floating-point numeric answer comparison; Number only parses the bounded exponent.
Equivalent fractions, decimal comma/dot, leading-dot decimals within present bound, scientific notation, signed numerator/denominator and Unicode minus.
24-digit integer accepted and 25 rejected; exponent +/-12 accepted, outside range rejected; zero denominator rejected in signed, decimal and exponent forms.
Anchored grammar rejects extra units, operators, mixed/grouping separators, base prefixes, Infinity, NaN and malformed expressions.
Blank/invalid/wrong remain distinct result kinds; correct=10, wrong=-1, invalid=-1, blank=0 in integer tenths.
96 normalized nonblank characters accepted in a valid padded fraction; 97 rejected.
250 exact rational equivalences and 250 one-unit numerator counterexamples produce correct/wrong as expected.
limits: The 96-character check applies after trim; all-whitespace input even longer than 96 is intentionally blank in the author test. It is not a cap on raw transport/string allocation.
24 digits refers to written mantissa digits per decimal part; fractions have two independently bounded parts. No unit conversion or tolerance is implemented.
Trailing decimal separator (1. or 1,) and choice strings with surrounding spaces are rejected by current explicit behavior; no silent normalization is inferred.

Selection still labels invalid-input policy UNDECIDED, while prototype assigns -1 tenth to invalid. This must become an explicit training decision before any user-facing integration; it is not a verified ministry rule.
Official completion acceptance/normalization remains unknown; these ten numerical training completions do not certify conformity to missing-word questions.

Initial failure log records a missing expected exception but does not preserve the initial failing source bytes; current numeric bad-key-on-blank case passes, broader key validation still fails as reproduced.
Proposed patch has been written for root review only and not applied or runtime-validated; no corrected implementation is claimed.
Input values outside TypeScript string type currently throw TypeError in places; proposed diff makes answer input invalid and key input an explicit error.
